     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Projective.RelativeProjectiveSpace
     7	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.ZariskisMainTheorem
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Projective morphisms
    11	
    12	This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that
    13	Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide. A morphism is projective when it factors as
    14	a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open CategoryTheory Limits
    18	
    19	noncomputable section
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    24	
    25	/-- A morphism is projective if it admits a closed immersion into a
    26	finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    27	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    28	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    29	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    30	
    31	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    32	
    33	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    34	
    35	/-- Projective morphisms are proper. -/
    36	theorem isProper (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsProper pi := by
    37	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    38	  letI : Finite n := hn
    39	  haveI := hi
    40	  rw [← hcomp]
    41	  infer_instance
    42	
    43	/-- Projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
    44	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi :=
    45	  haveI := h.isProper
    46	  inferInstance
    47	
    48	/-- Projective morphisms are separated. -/
    49	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsSeparated pi :=
    50	  haveI := h.isProper
    51	  inferInstance
    52	
    53	/-- Projective morphisms are universally closed. -/
    54	theorem universallyClosed (h : pi.IsProjective) : UniversallyClosed pi :=
    55	  haveI := h.isProper
    56	  inferInstance
    57	
    58	/-- A closed immersion into a projective scheme is projective. -/
    59	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : pi.IsProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    60	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] : (j ≫ pi).IsProjective := by
    61	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    62	  letI : Finite n := hn
    63	  haveI := hi
    64	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
    65	
    66	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed source to the corresponding
    67	base change of its ambient projective space. -/
    68	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
    69	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
    70	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
    71	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
    72	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
    73	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
    74	
    75	/-- Projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
    76	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    77	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsProjective := by
    78	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    79	  letI : Finite n := hn
    80	  haveI := hi
    81	  refine ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_⟩
    82	  · have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
    83	        pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
    84	    have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
    85	        (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
    86	      have hbig : IsPullback
    87	          (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
    88	          (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
    89	        rw [h1, hcomp]
    90	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
    91	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
    92	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
    93	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
    94	    exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi
    95	  · exact IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
    96	
    97	/-- A proper morphism that factors through projective space by an immersion is
    98	projective. Properness makes the immersion closed. -/
    99	theorem of_isProper_of_immersion (hpi : IsProper pi) {n : Type u} [Finite n]
   100	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hi : IsImmersion i)
   101	    (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) : pi.IsProjective := by
   102	  letI : IsImmersion i := hi
   103	  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := hcomp ▸ hpi
   104	  haveI : IsProper i := IsProper.of_comp i (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)
   105	  haveI : IsClosedImmersion i :=
   106	    (IsClosedImmersion.iff_isProper_and_mono (f := i)).mpr
   107	      ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
   108	  exact ⟨n, inferInstance, i, inferInstance, hcomp⟩
   109	
   110	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
   111	
   112	namespace ProjectiveSpace
   113	
   114	/-- The structural morphism of relative projective space is projective. -/
   115	theorem isProjective_over (n : Type u) [Finite n] (S : Scheme.{u}) :
   116	    (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S).IsProjective :=
   117	  ⟨n, inferInstance, 𝟙 _, inferInstance, Category.id_comp _⟩
   118	
   119	end ProjectiveSpace
   120	
   121	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtPointedReduction
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveMorphism
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CurveProjectivity
     9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.AmbientPicNotProper
    10	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StableAffineCover
    11	
    12	/-!
    13	# Quasi-projectivity, as the vocabulary `FiniteInAffine` was standing in for
    14	
    15	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`) says every finite
    16	subset of `X` lies in a single affine open.  It is the elementary, action-free form
    17	of the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis that the whole finite-Galois-quotient engine runs
    18	on, and up to now the project carried it **by hand**, with the same sentence
    19	written in three places: *"it holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no
    20	quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by
    21	hand"* (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`,
    22	`Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
    23	
    24	This file removes the hand: it derives `FiniteInAffine` from the project's
    25	finite-projective-space notion `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective`; projectivity is
    26	the closed-immersion special case.  The chain is
    27	
    28	  graded prime avoidance  ⟹  `FiniteInAffine (Proj 𝒜)`
    29	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine ℙ(n; S)`   (affine morphism descent)
    30	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine X` for `X` H-quasi-projective over `S`.
    31	
    32	## The two avoidance inputs
    33	
    34	The original deep input is the first step, and it is **absent from mathlib
    35	`v4.31`**: there is no *graded* prime avoidance.  Mathlib has
    36	`Ideal.subset_union_prime_finite` — a homogeneous ideal not contained in the union
    37	of finitely many primes is not contained in any one of them — but the element it
    38	produces is an arbitrary element of the ideal, while
    39	`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen` demands `f ∈ 𝒜 m` with `0 < m`.
    40	Getting a **homogeneous** avoiding element of **positive degree** is §1, and it is
    41	where the grading is consumed.
    42	
    43	For a closed immersion the final transport is cheap: `IsClosedImmersion →
    44	IsAffineHom`, and `IsAffineOpen.preimage` pulls affine opens back.  An open
    45	immersion needs a second prime-avoidance step: after placing the finite image in
    46	an affine open, `GaloisDescent.exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite` shrinks it to a
    47	basic open lying inside the immersion range.  The standard closed/open
    48	factorization then gives transport along every immersion.
    49	
    50	Thus graded avoidance is the new algebraic result in this file.  Open-immersion
    51	transport is the only additional substantive geometric step; its algebra is
    52	delegated to the already-landed finite prime-avoidance theorem.  The remaining
    53	H-quasi-projective and coproduct declarations are factorization and packaging.
    54	
    55	## What this does and does not buy
    56	
    57	It does **not** discharge the `FiniteInAffine` conjunct of
    58	`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep`.  That conjunct is about the **Picard scheme**, and
    59	nothing in this project produces an H-quasi-projective witness for the relevant
    60	Picard component.  Kleiman §5 `th:qpp&p` gives quasi-projectivity of `Pic^0`;
    61	formalizing and transporting that source theorem remains open.  What changes is the *kind* of thing
    62	that is open: the antecedent's last non-projection conjunct is now reducible to a
    63	standard geometric hypothesis with a standard proof, rather than an elementary
    64	condition invented here.  Stated as
    65	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjective` in §3.
    66	
    67	It **does** discharge, unconditionally and for free, the orbit hypothesis of the
    68	Galois-descent engine at every projective scheme
    69	(`Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_isProjective`), which is what
    70	`Picard/GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean` had only for *affine* `X` and what the
    71	Albanese lane's `OrbitsInAffineOpen` had for no `X` at all.  Smooth proper
    72	geometrically integral curves **are** projective in this project
    73	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`,
    74	`Picard/CurveProjectivity.lean`), so §3 fires at the curve itself with no
    75	hypothesis beyond its own binders.
    76	
    77	## What §5 is NOT: read this before consuming `PointedPicSharpRepProjective`
    78	
    79	§5 restates the seam's antecedent with `IsProjective` of the representing scheme in
    80	place of `FiniteInAffine`.  **That antecedent is refuted at the object it is about**,
    81	and the refutation is landed here as a theorem, not left as prose:
    82	`Scheme.not_isProjective_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`.  Projectivity over a field
    83	forces `IsProper`, hence `UniversallyClosed`, hence — over the compact `Spec k` —
    84	`CompactSpace` (`Scheme.compactSpace_of_isProjective`); and the full Picard scheme is a
    85	**disjoint union over `deg ∈ ℤ`** (Kleiman §6 `ex:curves`), which is not quasi-compact.
    86	So `PointedPicSharpRepProjective` is not the standard hypothesis restated — it is
    87	strictly stronger and false at `Pic_{C/k}`.
    88	
    89	This is verbatim the trap `Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean` exists to record, "trap (c):
    90	a `P → Q` whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting", and it is caught by
    91	that file's own theorems.  Kleiman's `th:qpp&p` gives quasi-projectivity of `Pic^0`,
    92	not projectivity of the ambient scheme.  §5 therefore survives only as a
    93	*conditional* reduction with an explicitly refuted antecedent; §3 and §4, which do not
    94	mention the ambient Picard scheme, are unaffected.
    95	
    96	An earlier revision of this section said §5 states the seam "with no condition invented
    97	in this project anywhere in it".  Both halves were wrong: `Scheme.Hom.IsProjective` is
    98	project-local (`Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`, mathlib `v4.31` has no
    99	morphism-level projectivity at all), as are `PicScheme.picSharp` and
   100	`Scheme.HasRationalPoint`; and the antecedent is not merely non-standard but refutable.
   101	The defensible statement is the narrow one: the *mathematical notion* is standard even
   102	though the Lean definition is ours.
   103	
   104	## Non-vacuity
   105	
   106	`FiniteInAffine` is satisfiable at an affine scheme with `⊤`
   107	(`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAffine`, already landed) and that witness is
   108	*degenerate*: it says nothing about the projective case.  So the honest
   109	non-degeneracy evidence for §2 is what a fresh-context audit could **verify**, and it
   110	is at `Proj`: `Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) ℚ)` is nonempty (the point
   111	`V(X₀)`), and the hypotheses of `Scheme.exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem` are jointly
   112	satisfiable there, both checked by elaborating them at that named object.
   113	
   114	**What is NOT verified, stated because an earlier revision of this paragraph asserted
   115	it as the ground of non-degeneracy:** that `ℙ(n; S)` fails to be affine for `n` with at
   116	least two elements.  It is true, but it is proved nowhere in mathlib at this pin
   117	(no `¬ IsAffine` results at all) nor in this project, so
   118	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace` being a *non-affine* witness rests on prose.
   119	That earlier revision also claimed the caution "is recorded as
   120	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace`"; that theorem records no such thing — it has no
   121	`Nonempty` hypothesis and no non-affineness content.
   122	-/

   132	/-! ## §1. Graded prime avoidance
   133	
   134	The new algebraic input.  The open-immersion theorem in §2 is the other
   135	substantive geometric step, delegating its algebra to `StableAffineCover`.
   136	-/
   137	
   138	section GradedAvoidance
   139	
   140	variable {σ : Type*} {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A]
   141	variable (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜]
   142	
   143	/-- **A finite `inf` of homogeneous ideals is homogeneous.** Bookkeeping for the
   144	avoidance argument, which needs `I ⊓ ⨅_{i ≠ j} p i` to be homogeneous in order to
   145	extract a homogeneous element from it. -/
   146	theorem Ideal.IsHomogeneous.finsetInf {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → Ideal A)
   147	    (h : ∀ i ∈ s, (p i).IsHomogeneous 𝒜) : (s.inf p).IsHomogeneous 𝒜 := by
   148	  classical
   149	  induction s using Finset.induction with
   150	  | empty =>
   151	      rw [Finset.inf_empty]
   152	      exact fun _ _ _ => Submodule.mem_top
   153	  | insert a t _ IH =>
   154	      rw [Finset.inf_insert]
   155	      exact fun i x hx =>
   156	        ⟨h a (Finset.mem_insert_self a t) i hx.1,
   157	          IH (fun j hj => h j (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hj)) i hx.2⟩
   158	
   159	/-- **Graded prime avoidance at a single relevant homogeneous prime.** If a
   160	homogeneous ideal `I` is not contained in a homogeneous prime `p`, and `p` does not
   161	contain the irrelevant ideal, then `I` has a homogeneous element of **strictly
   162	positive** degree outside `p`.
   163	
   164	Two separate uses of the grading, and it is worth naming both because the second is
   165	the one an ungraded intuition drops:
   166	
   167	* `I` homogeneous and `¬ I ≤ p` gives a homogeneous element of `I` outside `p` —
   168	  decompose a witness and note that if every component were in `p` so would the
   169	  witness be. Its degree is **not controlled** and may be `0`.
   170	* Relevance of `p` (`¬ 𝒜₊ ≤ p`) gives a homogeneous `g ∉ p` of positive degree, by
   171	  the same decomposition applied to a witness in the irrelevant ideal, whose
   172	  degree-`0` component is zero by definition.
   173	
   174	Then `f₀ * g` is homogeneous of degree `> 0`, lies in `I` (an ideal) and avoids `p`
   175	(a prime). Relevance is exactly what makes this possible: over a `p` containing
   176	`𝒜₊` — i.e. at a point *not* in `Proj` — every positive-degree homogeneous element
   177	lies in `p` and the conclusion is false. -/
   178	theorem exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem
   179	    {I p : Ideal A} [hp : p.IsPrime] (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
   180	    (hrel : ¬ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ p) (hIp : ¬ I ≤ p) :
   181	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ f ∈ I ∧ f ∉ p := by
   182	  classical
   183	  obtain ⟨n, f₀, hf₀deg, hf₀I, hf₀p⟩ : ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : A), f ∈ 𝒜 n ∧ f ∈ I ∧ f ∉ p := by
   184	    obtain ⟨x, hxI, hxp⟩ := SetLike.not_le_iff_exists.mp hIp
   185	    by_contra hcon
   186	    push Not at hcon
   187	    exact hxp (by
   188	      rw [← DirectSum.sum_support_decompose 𝒜 x]
   189	      refine Ideal.sum_mem _ fun i _ => ?_
   190	      by_contra h
   191	      exact h (hcon i _ (SetLike.coe_mem _) ((hI.mem_iff).mp hxI i)))
   192	  obtain ⟨m, g, hm, hgdeg, hgp⟩ : ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : A), 0 < m ∧ g ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ g ∉ p := by
   193	    obtain ⟨x, hxirr, hxp⟩ := SetLike.not_le_iff_exists.mp hrel
   194	    by_contra hcon
   195	    push Not at hcon
   196	    exact hxp (by
   197	      rw [← DirectSum.sum_support_decompose 𝒜 x]
   198	      refine Ideal.sum_mem _ fun i _ => ?_
   199	      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos i with rfl | hi
   200	      · have hz : (DirectSum.decompose 𝒜 x 0 : A) = 0 := by
   201	          have := (HomogeneousIdeal.mem_irrelevant_iff 𝒜 x).mp hxirr
   202	          simpa [GradedRing.proj_apply] using this
   203	        simp [hz]
   204	      · exact hcon i _ hi (SetLike.coe_mem _))
   205	  exact ⟨n + m, f₀ * g, by omega, SetLike.mul_mem_graded hf₀deg hgdeg,
   206	    I.mul_mem_right _ hf₀I, fun h => (hp.mem_or_mem h).elim hf₀p hgp⟩
   207	
   208	/-- **Graded prime avoidance for an incomparable family** — the case with the
   209	construction in it.
   210	
   211	Given finitely many pairwise-incomparable relevant homogeneous primes `q ∈ T`, none
   212	containing the homogeneous ideal `I`, there is a **single** homogeneous element of
   213	`I` of **positive** degree outside every one of them.
   214	
   215	The classical product/sum trick, with the grading forcing one extra step:
   216	
   217	* Incomparability makes `I ⊓ ⨅_{q' ∈ T, q' ≠ q} q'` not contained in `q` — if it
   218	  were, primality would put one of the factors inside `q`. So
   219	  `exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem` supplies, for each `q`, a homogeneous
   220	  `f q ∈ I` of positive degree `m q` that lies in every *other* member of `T` and
   221	  not in `q`.
   222	* Those degrees differ, so their sum need not be homogeneous. Equalise: with
   223	  `M := ∏ m q` each `m q` divides `M`, and `F q := (f q) ^ (M / m q)` is homogeneous
   224	  of the **common** degree `M > 0`, still in `I` and with the same membership
   225	  pattern (a prime contains a power iff it contains the base).
   226	* `∑_{q ∈ T} F q` is then homogeneous of degree `M`, lies in `I`, and modulo any
   227	  `q ∈ T` reduces to `F q ≠ 0 mod q` because every other summand is in `q`.
   228	
   229	This is the only place in the file where anything is constructed; §2 onwards is
   230	transport. -/
   231	theorem exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem_of_antichain
   232	    (T : Finset (Ideal A)) (hp : ∀ q ∈ T, q.IsPrime)
   233	    (hph : ∀ q ∈ T, q.IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
   234	    (hrel : ∀ q ∈ T, ¬ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ q)
   235	    (hanti : ∀ q ∈ T, ∀ q' ∈ T, q ≠ q' → ¬ q ≤ q')
   236	    {I : Ideal A} (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜) (hIp : ∀ q ∈ T, ¬ I ≤ q)
   237	    (hM : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ f ∈ I) :
   238	    ∃ (M : ℕ) (h : A), 0 < M ∧ h ∈ 𝒜 M ∧ h ∈ I ∧ ∀ q ∈ T, h ∉ q := by
   239	  classical
   240	  rcases T.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | hne
   241	  · obtain ⟨m, f, hm, hfd, hfI⟩ := hM
   242	    exact ⟨m, f, hm, hfd, hfI, by simp⟩
   243	  -- Choose, for each `q ∈ T`, a homogeneous positive-degree element of
   244	  -- `I ⊓ ⨅_{q' ≠ q} q'` outside `q`.
   245	  have key : ∀ q ∈ T, ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧
   246	      f ∈ (I ⊓ (T.erase q).inf id) ∧ f ∉ q := by
   247	    intro q hq
   248	    haveI := hp q hq
   249	    refine exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem 𝒜 (I := I ⊓ (T.erase q).inf id) ?_ (hrel q hq) ?_
   250	    · exact fun i x hx =>
   251	        ⟨hI i hx.1,
   252	          Ideal.IsHomogeneous.finsetInf 𝒜 _ id
   253	            (fun q' hq' => hph q' (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hq')) i hx.2⟩
   254	    · intro hle
   255	      rcases (hp q hq).inf_le.mp hle with h | h
   256	      · exact hIp q hq h
   257	      · obtain ⟨q', hq', hq'le⟩ := (hp q hq).inf_le'.mp h
   258	        exact hanti q' (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hq') q hq
   259	          (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hq') hq'le
   260	  choose! m f hmpos hfdeg hfmem hfout using key
   261	  have hfI : ∀ q ∈ T, f q ∈ I := fun q hq => (hfmem q hq).1
   262	  have hfin : ∀ q ∈ T, ∀ q' ∈ T.erase q, f q ∈ q' := fun q hq q' hq' =>
   263	    Finset.inf_le (f := id) hq' (hfmem q hq).2
   264	  -- Equalise the degrees: `M := ∏ m q`, and `F q := (f q) ^ (M / m q)` has degree `M`.
   265	  set M : ℕ := ∏ q ∈ T, m q with hMdef
   266	  have hMpos : 0 < M := Finset.prod_pos hmpos
   267	  have hquot : ∀ q ∈ T, 0 < M / m q := fun q hq =>
   268	    Nat.div_pos (Finset.single_le_prod' (fun i hi => hmpos i hi) hq) (hmpos q hq)
   269	  set F : Ideal A → A := fun q => (f q) ^ (M / m q) with hFdef
   270	  have hFdeg : ∀ q ∈ T, F q ∈ 𝒜 M := by
   271	    intro q hq
   272	    have h2 := SetLike.pow_mem_graded (M / m q) (hfdeg q hq)
   273	    rwa [smul_eq_mul, Nat.div_mul_cancel (Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem m hq)] at h2
   274	  have hFI : ∀ q ∈ T, F q ∈ I := fun q hq =>
   275	    Ideal.pow_mem_of_mem I (hfI q hq) _ (hquot q hq)
   276	  have hFin : ∀ q ∈ T, ∀ q' ∈ T.erase q, F q ∈ q' := fun q hq q' hq' =>
   277	    Ideal.pow_mem_of_mem _ (hfin q hq q' hq') _ (hquot q hq)
   278	  have hFout : ∀ q ∈ T, F q ∉ q := fun q hq hmem =>
   279	    hfout q hq ((hp q hq).mem_of_pow_mem _ hmem)
   280	  refine ⟨M, ∑ q ∈ T, F q, hMpos, sum_mem hFdeg,
   281	    Ideal.sum_mem _ fun q hq => hFI q hq, ?_⟩
   282	  intro q hq hmem
   283	  rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase T F hq] at hmem
   284	  have hrest : (∑ q' ∈ T.erase q, F q') ∈ q :=
   285	    Ideal.sum_mem _ fun q' hq' => hFin q' (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hq') q
   286	      (Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨(Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hq').symm, hq⟩)
   287	  exact hFout q hq ((Ideal.add_mem_iff_left _ hrest).mp hmem)
   288	
   289	/-- **Graded prime avoidance, general form** — the incomparability hypothesis of
   290	`exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem_of_antichain` removed.
   291	
   292	Any finite family of ideals is dominated by its **maximal** members, and avoiding
   293	those avoids all of them: if `f ∉ q` and `q' ≤ q` then `f ∉ q'`, since `f ∈ q'` would
   294	put `f` in `q`. The maximal members form an antichain by construction, so the
   295	previous theorem applies to them.
   296	
   297	Note the direction. It is the *maximal* primes that must be avoided, not the minimal
   298	ones — the inclusion runs the useful way only for a superset. Reducing to minimal
   299	primes, which is the reflex from the ungraded theory, would prove nothing here. -/
   300	theorem exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem
   301	    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → Ideal A)
   302	    (hp : ∀ i ∈ s, (p i).IsPrime) (hph : ∀ i ∈ s, (p i).IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
   303	    (hrel : ∀ i ∈ s, ¬ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ p i)
   304	    {I : Ideal A} (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜) (hIp : ∀ i ∈ s, ¬ I ≤ p i)
   305	    (hM : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ f ∈ I) :
   306	    ∃ (M : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < M ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 M ∧ f ∈ I ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, f ∉ p i := by
   307	  classical
   308	  set S : Finset (Ideal A) := s.image p with hS
   309	  set T : Finset (Ideal A) := S.filter (fun q => Maximal (fun x => x ∈ S) q) with hT
   310	  -- every member of `T` is one of the `p i`
   311	  have hTmem : ∀ q ∈ T, ∃ i ∈ s, q = p i := by
   312	    intro q hq
   313	    obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hq).1
   314	    exact ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩
   315	  -- every `p i` sits below some member of `T`
   316	  have hTdom : ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ q ∈ T, p i ≤ q := by
   317	    intro i hi
   318	    obtain ⟨q, hle, hmax⟩ := S.exists_le_maximal (Finset.mem_image_of_mem p hi)
   319	    exact ⟨q, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hmax.1, hmax⟩, hle⟩
   320	  obtain ⟨M, f, hMpos, hfdeg, hfI, hfout⟩ :=
   321	    exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem_of_antichain 𝒜 T
   322	      (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hp i hi)
   323	      (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hph i hi)
   324	      (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hrel i hi)
   325	      (fun q hq q' hq' hne hle =>
   326	        hne ((Finset.mem_filter.mp hq).2.eq_of_ge (Finset.mem_filter.mp hq').1 hle).symm)
   327	      hI (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hIp i hi) hM
   328	  refine ⟨M, f, hMpos, hfdeg, hfI, fun i hi hmem => ?_⟩
   329	  obtain ⟨q, hq, hle⟩ := hTdom i hi
   330	  exact hfout q hq (hle hmem)
   331	
   332	/-- **`Proj 𝒜` satisfies `FiniteInAffine`.** The geometric half of §1, and the first
   333	statement in the chain that is about a scheme.
   334	
   335	A point of `Proj 𝒜` *is* a relevant homogeneous prime, and "relevant" is literally the
   336	hypothesis `exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem` needs — the structure field
   337	`ProjectiveSpectrum.not_irrelevant_le` serves simultaneously as the relevance input
   338	and as `¬ I ≤ p x` for `I := 𝒜₊`. So with the irrelevant ideal as `I`, avoidance
   339	returns a homogeneous `f` of positive degree lying outside every one of the finitely
   340	many given points, i.e. `D₊(f)` contains them all; and `D₊(f)` is affine by
   341	`Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen`, whose `f ∈ 𝒜 m` and `0 < m` hypotheses are exactly what
   342	§1 was built to deliver.
   343	
   344	The degenerate case is handled by the same field: the non-degeneracy input (some
   345	positive-degree homogeneous element exists) is derived from *any* point of `Proj 𝒜`,
   346	and when there is no point the finite set is empty and any affine open serves. This is
   347	the finite generalisation of the argument mathlib runs one point at a time inside
   348	`Proj`'s own `local_affine` field. -/
   349	theorem _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finiteInAffine_proj :
   350	    Scheme.FiniteInAffine (Proj 𝒜) := by
   351	  classical
   352	  intro s hs
   353	  lift s to Finset (Proj 𝒜) using hs with t ht
   354	  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty (Proj 𝒜) with hem | ⟨⟨x₀⟩⟩
   355	  · exact ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top _⟩, fun x _ => (hem.false x).elim⟩
   356	  obtain ⟨M, f, hMpos, hfdeg, -, hfout⟩ :=
   357	    exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem 𝒜 t
   358	      (fun x => (x.asHomogeneousIdeal).toIdeal)
   359	      (fun x _ => x.isPrime)
   360	      (fun x _ => x.asHomogeneousIdeal.isHomogeneous)
   361	      (fun x _ => x.not_irrelevant_le)
   362	      (I := (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal)
   363	      (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).isHomogeneous
   364	      (fun x _ => x.not_irrelevant_le)
   365	      (by
   366	        obtain ⟨m, g, hm, hgdeg, -, -⟩ :=
   367	          exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem 𝒜
   368	            (I := (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal)
   369	            (p := (x₀.asHomogeneousIdeal).toIdeal)
   370	            (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).isHomogeneous
   371	            x₀.not_irrelevant_le x₀.not_irrelevant_le
   372	        exact ⟨m, g, hm, hgdeg, HomogeneousIdeal.mem_irrelevant_of_mem 𝒜 hm hgdeg⟩)
   373	  exact ⟨⟨Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f, Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen 𝒜 f hfdeg hMpos⟩,
   374	    fun x hx => hfout x (by exact_mod_cast hx)⟩
   375	
   376	end GradedAvoidance
   377	
   378	/-! ## §2. Descent along affine morphisms and immersions
   379	
   380	The affine and closed-immersion cases are transport.  The open-immersion case
   381	uses the independent finite prime-avoidance result from `StableAffineCover`; all
   382	later results are factorization or packaging.
   383	-/
   384	
   385	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` descends along any affine morphism.**
   386	
   387	The preimage of an affine open under an affine morphism is an affine open
   388	(`IsAffineOpen.preimage`), and a finite set upstairs has a finite image downstairs.
   389	So the property propagates in the direction that is useful for embeddings: from the
   390	ambient space to a subscheme.
   391	
   392	This generalises the already-landed `Scheme.finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom`
   393	(`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`), which is the special case `Y = Spec k`: there
   394	the conclusion came from `X` being outright affine, whereas here `Y` need only satisfy
   395	`FiniteInAffine`; relative projective space supplies the important application.
   396	That is the whole reason this direction is worth having as a separate lemma. -/
   397	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
   398	    (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
   399	  intro s hs
   400	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)

   769	`Pic_{C/k} = ∐_{d ∈ ℤ} Pic^d` is a countable disjoint union and projectivity of it would
   770	force `CompactSpace` (`compactSpace_of_isProjective`), which `Pic_{C/k}` is not
   771	(`not_isProjective_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`).  The usable replacement is a
   772	coproduct of components that each carry an H-quasi-projective witness.  Constructing
   773	those component witnesses is a separate producer obligation.
   774	
   775	`FiniteInAffine`, unlike `IsProjective` or `CompactSpace`, **is** closed under such
   776	coproducts: a finite set meets only finitely many components, each hit in an affine open,
   777	and finitely many disjoint affine opens have an affine `iSup`
   778	(`IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint`).  So this section turns the refuted globally-projective
   779	antecedent into a degree-graded substrate — `FiniteInAffine` of the ambient coproduct
   780	follows from H-quasi-projectivity of each supplied component, which is exactly the
   781	geometric adapter a future degree assembly can consume.  This file does not construct
   782	that assembly or any Picard representer.
   783	
   784	Everything here is about coproducts of arbitrary schemes and carries **no** hypothesis
   785	about the curve; nothing closes the seam.  It is the substrate the earlier sections said
   786	was missing ("degree-invariance of the semilinear action, together with the degree-graded
   787	decomposition of `PicSchemeEt`" — the second half). -/
   788	
   789	section Coproduct
   790	
   791	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` is closed under arbitrary set-indexed coproducts.**  If every
   792	component scheme `g i` satisfies `FiniteInAffine`, so does `∐ g`.
   793	
   794	A finite `s ⊆ ∐ g` meets only the finitely many components indexed by `idx '' s`; within
   795	each, `s` pulls back along the open immersion `Sigma.ι g i` to a finite set covered by an
   796	affine open `U i`; the images `Sigma.ι g i ''ᵁ U i` are pairwise disjoint
   797	(`disjoint_opensRange_sigmaι`) affine opens (image of an affine open under an open
   798	immersion), so their finite `iSup` is affine (`IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint`) and
   799	contains `s`.
   800	
   801	This is the property `§5.5`'s refutation identified as the one the degree-graded Picard
   802	scheme has and global projectivity does not. -/
   803	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] (g : σ → Scheme.{u})
   804	    (h : ∀ i, FiniteInAffine (g i)) : FiniteInAffine (∐ g) := by
   805	  classical
   806	  letI : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (Sigma.ι g i) := fun i =>
   807	    Scheme.IsLocallyDirected.instIsOpenImmersionι (Discrete.functor g) { as := i }
   808	  intro s hs
   809	  have hcomp : ∀ x : (∐ g : Scheme.{u}), ∃ i, x ∈ Set.range (Sigma.ι g i).base := by
   810	    intro x
   811	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := (sigmaOpenCover g).exists_eq x
   812	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
   813	  choose idx hidx using hcomp
   814	  have hpre : ∀ i : σ, ((Sigma.ι g i).base ⁻¹' s).Finite := fun i =>
   815	    hs.preimage ((Sigma.ι g i).isOpenEmbedding.injective).injOn
   816	  choose U hU using fun i => h i _ (hpre i)
   817	  set J : Set σ := idx '' s with hJ
   818	  have hJfin : J.Finite := hs.image idx
   819	  refine ⟨⟨⨆ i ∈ J, (Sigma.ι g i) ''ᵁ (U i).1, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
   820	  · apply IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint hJfin
   821	    · intro i _
   822	      exact (U i).2.image_of_isOpenImmersion _
   823	    · intro i _ j _ hij
   824	      exact Disjoint.mono (Scheme.Hom.image_le_opensRange _ _)
   825	        (Scheme.Hom.image_le_opensRange _ _) (disjoint_opensRange_sigmaι g i j hij)
   826	  · intro x hx
   827	    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hidx x
   828	    have hyU : y ∈ (U (idx x)).1 := by
   829	      apply hU (idx x)
   830	      simp only [Set.mem_preimage, hy]
   831	      exact hx
   832	    have hmem : x ∈ (Sigma.ι g (idx x)) ''ᵁ (U (idx x)).1 := ⟨y, hyU, hy⟩
   833	    exact (le_iSup₂ (f := fun i _ => (Sigma.ι g i) ''ᵁ (U i).1) (idx x)
   834	      ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩) hmem
   835	
   836	/-- A coproduct of schemes that are projective over one affine base satisfies
   837	`FiniteInAffine`. This is the degree-piece bridge: projectivity is checked on
   838	each component, while `FiniteInAffine` is concluded for their possibly infinite
   839	coproduct. -/
   840	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjective
   841	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
   842	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsProjective) :
   843	    FiniteInAffine (∐ fun i => (X i).left) :=
   844	  finiteInAffine_sigma _ fun i => finiteInAffine_of_isProjective (hX i)
   845	
   846	/-- A coproduct of H-quasi-projective schemes over one affine base satisfies
   847	`FiniteInAffine`, even when the coproduct itself is not quasi-compact. -/
   848	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective
   849	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
   850	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsHQuasiProjective) :
   851	    FiniteInAffine (∐ fun i => (X i).left) :=
   852	  finiteInAffine_sigma _ fun i => finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjective (hX i)
   853	
   854	/-- The carried very-ample form of `finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjective`.
   855	At `Scheme.{0}`, `IsProjectiveWith` records a line bundle together with its
   856	closed immersion into relative projective space; forgetting those certificates
   857	piecewise gives `FiniteInAffine` for the coproduct. -/
   858	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjectiveWith
   859	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{0, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{0}} [IsAffine S]
   860	    (X : σ → Over S) (L : ∀ i, (X i).left.Modules)
   861	    (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsProjectiveWith (L i)) :
   862	    FiniteInAffine (∐ fun i => (X i).left) :=
   863	  finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjective X fun i => (hX i).isProjective
   864	
   865	/-- The carried relatively very ample form of
   866	`finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective`. -/
   867	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjectiveWith
   868	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{0, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{0}} [IsAffine S]
   869	    (X : σ → Over S) (L : ∀ i, (X i).left.Modules)
   870	    (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsHQuasiProjectiveWith (L i)) :
   871	    FiniteInAffine (∐ fun i => (X i).left) :=
   872	  finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective X fun i =>
   873	    (hX i).isHQuasiProjective
   874	
   875	/-- A coproduct in `Over S` is locally of finite type when each of its
   876	components is. The proof compares its structure morphism with the descent
   877	morphism from the coproduct of the underlying schemes and uses that
   878	`LocallyOfFiniteType` is Zariski-local at the source. -/
   879	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_sigma
   880	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}}
   881	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (X i).hom) :
   882	    LocallyOfFiniteType (∐ X).hom := by
   883	  have hhom : (∐ X).hom = (PreservesCoproduct.iso (Over.forget S) X).hom ≫
   884	      Sigma.desc (fun i => (X i).hom) := by
   885	    haveI : HasColimit (Discrete.functor X ⋙ Over.forget S) :=
   886	      hasColimit_of_iso (F := Discrete.functor (fun i => (X i).left))
   887	        (Discrete.natIso (fun i => Iso.refl _))
   888	    refine (PreservesCoproduct.iso (Over.forget S) X).inv_comp_eq.mp ?_
   889	    rw [PreservesCoproduct.inv_hom]
   890	    refine Sigma.hom_ext _ _ fun i => ?_
   891	    rw [ι_comp_sigmaComparison_assoc, Sigma.ι_desc]
   892	    exact Over.w (Sigma.ι X i)
   893	  rw [hhom]
   894	  exact MorphismProperty.comp_mem @LocallyOfFiniteType
   895	    (PreservesCoproduct.iso (Over.forget S) X).hom
   896	    (Sigma.desc fun i => (X i).hom)
   897	    (by infer_instance)
   898	    (IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) hX)
   899	
   900	/-- The underlying scheme of the canonical coproduct in `Over S` inherits
   901	`FiniteInAffine` from its components.  This comparison lemma is independent of
   902	projectivity and is the reusable coproduct boundary. -/
   903	theorem finiteInAffine_over_sigma
   904	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}}
   905	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, FiniteInAffine (X i).left) :
   906	    FiniteInAffine (∐ X).left :=
   907	  finiteInAffine_of_iso (PreservesCoproduct.iso (Over.forget S) X).symm
   908	    (finiteInAffine_sigma _ hX)
   909	
   910	/-- The canonical coproduct in `Over S` satisfies `FiniteInAffine` when every
   911	component is projective over the affine base. This is the form used by a
   912	degree-piece representability assembly; `Over.forget S` identifies its
   913	underlying scheme with the coproduct handled by
   914	`finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjective`. -/
   915	theorem finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isProjective
   916	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
   917	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsProjective) :
   918	    FiniteInAffine (∐ X).left :=
   919	  finiteInAffine_over_sigma X fun i => finiteInAffine_of_isProjective (hX i)
   920	
   921	/-- The canonical coproduct in `Over S` satisfies `FiniteInAffine` when each
   922	component is H-quasi-projective over the affine base. -/
   923	theorem finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective
   924	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
   925	    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsHQuasiProjective) :
   926	    FiniteInAffine (∐ X).left :=
   927	  finiteInAffine_over_sigma X fun i =>
   928	    finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjective (hX i)
   929	
   930	/-- Very-ample projective degree pieces supply the two geometric side
   931	conditions required of their canonical coproduct by `PointedPicSharpRep`:
   932	local finite type of its structure morphism and `FiniteInAffine` of its
   933	underlying scheme. No representability hypothesis is introduced here. -/
   934	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_and_finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjectiveWith
   935	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{0, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{0}} [IsAffine S]
   936	    (X : σ → Over S) (L : ∀ i, (X i).left.Modules)
   937	    (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsProjectiveWith (L i)) :
   938	    LocallyOfFiniteType (∐ X).hom ∧ FiniteInAffine (∐ X).left :=
   939	  ⟨locallyOfFiniteType_sigma X fun i => (hX i).locallyOfFiniteType,
   940	    finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isProjective X fun i => (hX i).isProjective⟩
   941	
   942	/-- H-quasi-projective degree pieces carrying specified relatively very ample
   943	line bundles supply the two geometric side conditions for their canonical
   944	coproduct: local finite type and `FiniteInAffine`.  The theorem deliberately
   945	introduces no representability hypothesis; constructing the Picard degree
   946	pieces remains a separate producer obligation. -/
   947	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_and_finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjectiveWith
   948	    {σ : Type v} [Small.{0, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{0}} [IsAffine S]
   949	    (X : σ → Over S) (L : ∀ i, (X i).left.Modules)
   950	    (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsHQuasiProjectiveWith (L i)) :
   951	    LocallyOfFiniteType (∐ X).hom ∧ FiniteInAffine (∐ X).left :=
   952	  ⟨locallyOfFiniteType_sigma X fun i => (hX i).locallyOfFiniteType,
   953	    finiteInAffine_over_sigma X fun i =>
   954	      finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjectiveWith (hX i)⟩
   955	
   956	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` is closed under binary coproducts.**  The two-piece case of
   957	`finiteInAffine_sigma`, via `coprodIsoSigma` and the landed
   958	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_iso` (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`). -/
   959	theorem finiteInAffine_coprod {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (hX : FiniteInAffine X)
   960	    (hY : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine (X ⨿ Y) := by
   961	  refine finiteInAffine_of_iso (coprodIsoSigma X Y).symm ?_
   962	  apply finiteInAffine_sigma
   963	  rintro ⟨i⟩
   964	  cases i
   965	  · simpa using hX
   966	  · simpa using hY
   967	
   968	end Coproduct

    10	# The concrete project-local model of the admissible divisor representer
    11	
    12	The admissible coverage parameter is strictly positive, so the chosen representer in
    13	`DivRepAffChallenge` is definitionally the nonzero `DivScheme` branch.  This file names that
    14	concrete branch and transports its closed immersion into the Grassmannian pair back to
    15	`divRepAffAdmissibleScheme`.

    17	The resulting certificate is unconditional and geometric: the target has its finite affine
    18	product atlas, and the source is quasi-compact, locally of finite type, and separated over the
    19	base field.  It is not yet a finite-projective-space immersion.  That stronger conclusion needs
    20	the Plucker embeddings of both Grassmannian factors together with their Segre product; those
    21	maps are not present in the rebuild project.

   191	    (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowRankOne C)
   192	    (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowRankTwo C)

   197	      (divRepAffAdmissibleGrassmannianPair C).left := by

   212	    (windowM_choice (divRepAffP1Map C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp_over C)
   213	      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) • fiberWeilDivisor (divRepAffP1Map C))
   214	    (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)
   215	    (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowRankOne C) (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowRankTwo C)
   216	    (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowBasisOne C)

   219	        (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)).symm)
   220	
   221	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency true in

   223	-- The raw name keeps the dependent chosen bases out of downstream target types.
   224	/-- The raw admissible divisor embedding is a closed immersion. -/

   226	    IsClosedImmersion (divRepAffAdmissibleRawEmbedding C) := by

   238	  change IsClosedImmersion (divSchemeι k
   239	    (windowS_choice (divRepAffP1Map C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp_over C)
   240	      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) • fiberWeilDivisor (divRepAffP1Map C))
   241	    (windowM_choice (divRepAffP1Map C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp_over C)
   242	      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) • fiberWeilDivisor (divRepAffP1Map C))
   243	    (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)
   244	    (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowRankOne C) (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowRankTwo C)
   245	    (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowBasisOne C)
   246	    ((divRepAffAdmissibleWindowBasisTwo C).map
   247	      (windowShiftEquiv (divRepAffP1Map_comp_over C)
   248	        (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)).symm))
   249	  exact isClosedImmersion_divSchemeι k _ _ _ _ _ _ _
   250	
   251	/-- The concrete closed immersion of the admissible divisor model into its two-window
   252	Grassmannian pair. -/
   253	noncomputable def divRepAffAdmissibleConcreteEmbedding :
   254	    divRepAffAdmissibleConcreteScheme C ⟶
   255	      divRepAffAdmissibleGrassmannianPair C := by
   256	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := admissibleDivisorOver C
   257	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   258	    admissibleDivisorSmooth C
   259	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := admissibleDivisorIntegral C
   260	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   261	    admissibleDivisorLocallyOfFiniteType C
   262	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) := admissibleDivisorQuasiCompact C
   263	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
   264	    admissibleDivisorHModuleFiniteZero C
   265	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
   266	    admissibleDivisorHModuleFiniteOne C
   267	  refine Over.homMk (divRepAffAdmissibleRawEmbedding C) ?_
   268	  rfl
   269	
   270	/-- The concrete admissible divisor embedding is a closed immersion. -/
   271	theorem isClosedImmersion_divRepAffAdmissibleConcreteEmbedding :
   272	    IsClosedImmersion (divRepAffAdmissibleConcreteEmbedding C).left := by
   273	  change IsClosedImmersion (divRepAffAdmissibleRawEmbedding C)
   274	  exact isClosedImmersion_divRepAffAdmissibleRawEmbedding C
   275	
   276	/-- The actual chosen representer, not merely its concrete spelling, embeds into the
   277	Grassmannian pair. -/
   278	noncomputable def divRepAffAdmissibleEmbedding :
   279	    divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C ⟶ divRepAffAdmissibleGrassmannianPair C :=
   280	  eqToHom (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme_eq_concrete C) ≫
   281	    divRepAffAdmissibleConcreteEmbedding C
   282	
   283	/-- The embedding of the actual chosen admissible representer is a closed immersion. -/
   284	theorem isClosedImmersion_divRepAffAdmissibleEmbedding :
   285	    IsClosedImmersion (divRepAffAdmissibleEmbedding C).left := by
   286	  letI : IsClosedImmersion (divRepAffAdmissibleConcreteEmbedding C).left :=
   287	    isClosedImmersion_divRepAffAdmissibleConcreteEmbedding C
   288	  unfold divRepAffAdmissibleEmbedding
   289	  rw [Over.comp_left]
   290	  infer_instance
   291	
   292	/-- The admissible Grassmannian pair has the finite product frame atlas used by the divisor
   293	construction. -/
   294	noncomputable def divRepAffAdmissibleGrassmannianCover :
   295	    (divRepAffAdmissibleGrassmannianPair C).left.OpenCover :=
   296	  grPairCover k
   297	    (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowRankOne C)

   304	    (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowRankTwo C)
   305

   308	    (ij : (divRepAffAdmissibleGrassmannianCover C).I₀) :
   309	    IsAffine ((divRepAffAdmissibleGrassmannianCover C).X ij) :=
   310	  isAffine_grPairCover_X k
   311	    (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowRankOne C)
   312	    (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (divRepAffAdmissibleWindowRankTwo C) ij
   313	
   314	/-- The chosen admissible divisor source is quasi-compact over `k`. -/
   315	theorem quasiCompact_divRepAffAdmissibleScheme :
   316	    QuasiCompact (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom := by
   317	  rw [divRepAffAdmissibleScheme_eq_concrete]
   318	  unfold divRepAffAdmissibleConcreteScheme

   323	    LocallyOfFiniteType (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom := by
   324	  rw [divRepAffAdmissibleScheme_eq_concrete]
   325	  unfold divRepAffAdmissibleConcreteScheme
   326	  infer_instance

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The finite-stage Picard glue as a scheme over its field of definition
    10	
    11	The finite-stage glue package already contains affine algebras over its final finite
    12	subextension `P.N.1`.  Their structure maps agree on overlaps, so they descend to the
    13	glued scheme.  This retains the finite-stage object over `Spec P.N.1`, which is the
    14	object-level input for the scalar-extension comparison with the separably closed atlas.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    22	open scoped TensorProduct
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    29	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    30	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    31	
    32	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    33	
    34	set_option linter.style.setOption false
    35	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    36	-- Projecting the dependent scalar towers from `P` requires a larger local synthesis budget.
    37	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    38	/-- The structure map from the finite-stage glued scheme to its field of definition. -/
    39	noncomputable def gluedMap
    40	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    41	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    42	    P.glueData.glued ⟶ Spec (.of P.N.1) := by
    43	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
    44	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
    45	  let A : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u := fun U =>
    46	    Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U
    47	  let B : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u :=
    48	    fun U V =>
    49	      Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V
    50	  let r : ∀ U V, A U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    51	    pic0FiniteStageRestrictionBaseChange
    52	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
    53	  letI : ∀ U V, Algebra (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    54	    pic0FiniteStageAlgebraOfMap (r U V)
    55	  letI : ∀ U V, IsScalarTower P.N.1 (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    56	    pic0FiniteStageTowerOfMap (r U V)
    57	  let tau : ∀ U V, B V U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    58	    pic0FiniteStageTransitionBaseChange
    59	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
    60	  fapply Multicoequalizer.desc
    61	  · intro U
    62	    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U
    63	    exact Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U)))
    64	  · rintro ⟨U, V⟩
    65	    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U V
    66	    change
    67	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A U) (B U V))) ≫
    68	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U))) =
    69	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (tau U V).toRingHom) ≫
    70	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A V) (B V U)))) ≫
    71	            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A V)))
    72	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    73	    rw [Category.assoc, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    74	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    75	    congr 1
    76	    ext x
    77	    simp only [CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, CommRingCat.hom_comp,
    78	      ConcreteCategory.hom_ofHom, RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply,
    79	      AlgHom.toRingHom_eq_coe, Category.assoc, RingHom.coe_coe]
    80	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A U) (B U V)]
    81	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A V) (B V U)]
    82	    exact (tau U V).commutes x |>.symm
    83	
    84	/-- The finite-stage Picard glue, retained over the finite field `P.N.1`. -/
    85	noncomputable def gluedOver
    86	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    87	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) : Over (Spec (.of P.N.1)) :=
    88	  Over.mk P.gluedMap
    89	
    90	end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    91	
    92	end
    93	
    94	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import Mathlib
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveMorphismBasic
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SerreTwist
     9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.QuotFunctorDef
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# Projective and H-quasi-projective morphisms carrying a very ample line bundle
    13	
    14	Mathlib v4.31 has no projective-morphism class and no (very) ampleness
    15	vocabulary.  Following the encoding settled in inbox `I-0118` (comment
    16	`C-0002`), this file defines:
    17	
    18	* `ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n₀ S m` — the Serre twist `O(m)` on the
    19	  relative projective space `ℙ(n₀; S)`, the pullback of
    20	  `ProjTwist.serreTwist` from the integral model along `toProjInt`;
    21	* `ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheafBaseChange` — `O(m)` commutes with base
    22	  change of the ambient projective space;
    23	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith π L` — the **projective-with-`L`** predicate:
    24	  `π : X ⟶ S` factors through a closed immersion `i : X ↪ ℙ(n; S)` for a
    25	  finite coordinate type `n`, over `S` with `L ≅ i^* O(1)`;
    26	* `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjectiveWith π L` — the corresponding
    27	  **H-quasi-projective-with-`L`** predicate, with a quasi-compact immersion into
    28	  finite projective space and the same `O(1)` comparison.
    29	
    30	with the stability facts the Quot-scheme endgame consumes:
    31	
    32	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.isProper` — projective morphisms are proper;
    33	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.comp_isClosedImmersion` — a closed immersion
    34	  into a projective scheme is projective (carrying the restricted bundle);
    35	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.baseChange` — stability under base change
    36	  (carrying the pulled-back bundle).
    37	
    38	The `IsHQuasiProjectiveWith` terminology records the finite-projective-space
    39	convention.  No equivalence with every relative ample formulation over an
    40	arbitrary base is asserted here.
    41	
    42	The ampleness predicates and their carried-bundle stability theorems are at
    43	`Scheme.{0}`: the Serre twist rests on the descent engine
    44	`Scheme.Modules.glue`, which is universe-monomorphic at `Scheme.GlueData.{0}`
    45	(`GlueDescent.lean:934`).  The purely scheme-theoretic open-image isomorphism is
    46	universe-polymorphic.
    47	
    48	Blueprint: `def:twisting_sheaf`, `def:projective_with`,
    49	`lem:projective_with_proper`, `lem:projective_with_closed_immersion`,
    50	`lem:projective_with_base_change`
    51	(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
    52	-/
    53	
    54	open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial
    55	
    56	noncomputable section
    57	
    58	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    59	
    60	namespace ProjectiveSpace
    61	
    62	variable (n₀ : Type) (S : Scheme.{0})
    63	
    64	/-- The Serre twist `O(m)` on the relative projective space `ℙ(n₀; S)`:
    65	the pullback of the glued twisting sheaf on the integral model. -/
    66	def twistingSheaf (m : ℕ) : (ℙ(n₀; S)).Modules :=
    67	  (Scheme.Modules.pullback (toProjInt n₀ S)).obj (ProjTwist.serreTwist n₀ m)
    68	
    69	variable {S} {S' : Scheme.{0}}
    70	
    71	/-- The Serre twist commutes with base change of the ambient projective
    72	space: `(map g)^* O(m) ≅ O(m)`. -/
    73	def twistingSheafBaseChange (g : S' ⟶ S) (m : ℕ) :
    74	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (map n₀ g)).obj (twistingSheaf n₀ S m) ≅
    75	      twistingSheaf n₀ S' m :=
    76	  Scheme.pullbackTriangleIso (map_toProjInt n₀ g) (ProjTwist.serreTwist n₀ m)
    77	
    78	end ProjectiveSpace
    79	
    80	/-- `π : X ⟶ S` is a **projective morphism carrying the line bundle `L`**
    81	([Nitsure] §5, [EGA II] 5.5): there are a finite coordinate type `n`, a closed
    82	immersion `i : X ↪ ℙ(n; S)` over `S`, and an isomorphism of `L` with the
    83	pullback of the Serre twist `O(1)`.  This is the faithful encoding of
    84	"projective with relatively very ample `L`" settled in inbox `I-0118`. -/
    85	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith {X S : Scheme.{0}} (π : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules) :
    86	    Prop :=
    87	  ∃ (n : Type) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    88	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = π ∧
    89	      Nonempty (L ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj
    90	        (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n S 1))
    91	
    92	/-- `π : X ⟶ S` is **H-quasi-projective carrying `L`** if it admits a
    93	quasi-compact immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space,
    94	over `S`, which identifies `L` with the pullback of `O(1)`.  This is the
    95	project-local encoding of a specified relatively very ample line bundle. -/
    96	def Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjectiveWith {X S : Scheme.{0}} (π : X ⟶ S)
    97	    (L : X.Modules) : Prop :=
    98	  ∃ (n : Type) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    99	    IsImmersion i ∧ QuasiCompact i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = π ∧
   100	      Nonempty (L ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj
   101	        (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n S 1))
   102	
   103	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
   104	
   105	variable {X S : Scheme.{0}} {π : X ⟶ S}
   106	
   107	/-- Every projective morphism carries a relatively very ample line bundle: choose the
   108	pullback of `O(1)` along the closed immersion in the `IsProjective` witness. -/
   109	theorem exists_isProjectiveWith (h : π.IsProjective) :
   110	    ∃ L : X.Modules, π.IsProjectiveWith L := by
   111	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
   112	  letI : Finite n := hn
   113	  let L := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj
   114	    (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n S 1)
   115	  exact ⟨L, n, inferInstance, i, hi, hcomp, ⟨Iso.refl _⟩⟩
   116	
   117	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
   118	
   119	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith
   120	
   121	variable {X S : Scheme.{0}} {π : X ⟶ S} {L : X.Modules}
   122	
   123	/-- Forget the chosen very ample line bundle from a projective morphism. -/
   124	theorem isProjective (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : π.IsProjective := by
   125	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, -⟩ := h
   126	  exact ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩
   127	
   128	/-- A projective morphism carrying `L` is H-quasi-projective carrying the same
   129	line bundle. -/
   130	theorem isHQuasiProjectiveWith (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) :
   131	    π.IsHQuasiProjectiveWith L := by
   132	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, hL⟩ := h
   133	  letI : Finite n := hn
   134	  haveI : IsClosedImmersion i := hi
   135	  exact ⟨n, hn, i, inferInstance, inferInstance, hcomp, hL⟩
   136	
   137	/-- **Projective morphisms are proper**: a closed immersion is proper, the
   138	structural morphism of projective space is proper, and properness is stable
   139	under composition. -/
   140	theorem isProper (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : IsProper π := by
   141	  exact h.isProjective.isProper
   142	
   143	/-- **Projective morphisms are locally of finite type**: immediate from
   144	`isProper`, since properness extends `LocallyOfFiniteType`.  This lets the
   145	Quot-scheme endgame and the Hilbert-polynomial existence theorem derive finite
   146	type from projectivity instead of carrying it as a separate hypothesis. -/
   147	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : LocallyOfFiniteType π :=
   148	  haveI := h.isProper; inferInstance
   149	
   150	/-- **Projective morphisms are separated** (properness extends `IsSeparated`). -/
   151	theorem isSeparated (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : IsSeparated π :=
   152	  haveI := h.isProper; inferInstance
   153	
   154	/-- **Projective morphisms are universally closed** (properness extends
   155	`UniversallyClosed`). -/
   156	theorem universallyClosed (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : UniversallyClosed π :=
   157	  haveI := h.isProper; inferInstance
   158	
   159	/-- **Transfer along an isomorphism of the carried bundle**: `IsProjectiveWith`
   160	depends on `L` only up to isomorphism (it records the comparison `L ≅ i^* O(1)`
   161	through `Nonempty`), so if `π` is projective carrying `L` and `L ≅ L'`, then `π`
   162	is projective carrying `L'`.  Useful for consumers that only have the bundle up
   163	to isomorphism. -/
   164	theorem of_iso (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) {L' : X.Modules} (e : L ≅ L') :
   165	    π.IsProjectiveWith L' := by
   166	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, ⟨eL⟩⟩ := h
   167	  exact ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, ⟨e.symm ≪≫ eL⟩⟩
   168	
   169	/-- **Composition with a closed immersion**: if `π` is projective carrying
   170	`L` and `j` is a closed immersion into `X`, then `j ≫ π` is projective
   171	carrying `j^* L`. -/
   172	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) {Y : Scheme.{0}}
   173	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] :
   174	    (j ≫ π).IsProjectiveWith ((Scheme.Modules.pullback j).obj L) := by
